papers.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
papers.authors_short: Collins, De Groote, Gregg, Huang, Lenzi, Sartori, Sawicki, Si, Slade, Young
papers.venue: bioRxiv preprint ('contradictory results'), v1 posted 2026-04-06; bioRxiv API lists no journal version
papers.code_status: Replication data+code (DC2) and power-calculation code (DC1) posted as bioRxiv supplementary zip files
papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Ten biomechanics and robotics researchers argue Luo et al. 2024's simulation-trained exoskeleton gains are implausible: implied metabolic saving per joule of device work (5.5 walking, 6.6 stairs) exceeds physiological limits; their N=10 hardware replication of the average torque found no significant saving; code unreleased.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: gate every headline gain with a pre-registered physical-plausibility check (e.g., metabolic saving per joule of device work) and ship code, reward, seeds and all-seed learning curves with the claim.
papers.left_untested: The replication applied the average torque trajectory, not Luo's unreported learned policy, with four fixed timing shifts on a 4.8 kg device; it tests the torque profile, not learning-in-simulation. Not yet peer-reviewed.
papers.feasibility_notes: Short main text plus supplement; the energy-ratio calculation is cheap to reproduce and can run as an automatic gate on simulated gains.

papers.title: Empirical Design in Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_status: n/a (methods guide; no accompanying repository linked in the paper)
papers.core_idea: Practical guide to RL experiments: statistical assumptions behind performance measures, confidence and tolerance intervals, hypothesis tests, fair comparisons of several agents with equal tuning effort, and maximization bias from reporting the best hyperparameters. A 30-seed re-run of SAC versus DDPG reaches very different conclusions.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: two-stage protocol. Sweep on tuning seeds, freeze the chosen config, rerun it on a new, larger seed set and report only stage two; every arm, SMAT and simple baselines, gets the same tuning budget.
papers.left_untested: Examples use small classic-control and MuJoCo agents; no co-adapting human and device policies, staged curricula, or equivalence and non-inferiority tests with pre-set margins.
papers.feasibility_notes: Implementable in the scheduler; stage-two reruns on fresh seeds add a fixed compute cost per claim, so reserve it when queuing.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
papers.code_status: released (rliable library, pip-installable); GitHub repo now archived (read-only)
papers.api_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
papers.core_idea: With few runs per task, point estimates of mean or median scores mislead. Report stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals, interquartile mean, performance profiles and probability of improvement; re-analysis of Atari 100k and other benchmarks shows published conclusions change once uncertainty is counted.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: every reported number carries a bootstrap 95% CI over independent seeds, with all runs included; headline aggregates use IQM and performance profiles, never a single best seed.
papers.left_untested: Designed for many-task suites; SMAT and sprint studies have few tasks and paired human-device outcomes, and the paper sets no equivalence margins or decision rules for 'same as baseline'.
papers.feasibility_notes: pip-installable, negligible cost; usable with 5-10 seeds per arm, which fits one GPU.

papers.title: Equivalence Testing for Psychological Research: A Tutorial
papers.venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 1(2):259-269
papers.code_status: TOSTER R package by the first author (maintained; last push Sept 2026)
papers.api_title: Equivalence Testing for Psychological Research: A Tutorial
papers.core_idea: Tutorial on the two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure for rejecting effects as large as a smallest effect size of interest (SESOI). Reviews ways to justify the SESOI, combines equivalence with null-hypothesis tests, and gives worked reporting examples.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: fix the SESOI in raw units (seconds of sprint time, % metabolic cost) before results; verdicts come from the combined TOST and difference-test outcomes; 'not significant' alone never means 'same'.
papers.left_untested: Human-sample psychology examples; nothing on random seeds as the replication unit, dependence among runs, or deriving a reproduction margin from an original paper's reported effect.
papers.feasibility_notes: No compute; TOSTER or two one-sided Welch t-tests in Python (90% CI) implement it.

papers.title: The preregistration revolution
papers.core_idea: Testing predictions on new observations differs from postdiction (explaining data already seen); hindsight bias blurs them. Preregistering research questions and analysis plan before seeing outcomes separates the two; the paper gives strategies for imperfect cases such as preexisting data.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: each queued config carries a timestamped, hashed plan (hypothesis, metric, tolerance, seeds, analysis) frozen before any result; deviations are logged and affected results relabelled exploratory.
papers.left_untested: Written for human-subject science; silent on automated agents that generate and queue many hypotheses, and on how many preregistered comparisons a sweep may spend.
papers.feasibility_notes: Pure process: an append-only ledger entry at queue time, checked at report time.

papers.title: Hyperparameters in Reinforcement Learning and How To Tune Them
papers.code_status: released (Hydra sweepers for DEHB and PBT variants); repo archived
papers.api_title: Hyperparameters in Reinforcement Learning and How To Tune Them
papers.core_idea: RL hyperparameters strongly change results, and the best configuration depends on the tuning seed, so tuned incumbents overfit their seeds. HPO tools (DEHB, PBT variants, random search) often beat hand-tuning at lower cost; recommends separate tuning and test seeds and reported search spaces.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: tuning seeds and evaluation seeds are disjoint sets fixed at pre-registration; the runner refuses to report any number computed on a seed that touched tuning or checkpoint selection.
papers.left_untested: Single-agent benchmarks (Acrobot, Pendulum, MiniGrid, Brax, Procgen); no co-adapting human and device agents, staged curricula, or equivalence tests between tuned methods.
papers.feasibility_notes: Released sweepers plug into Hydra; random search over a declared space with disjoint seeds is affordable on one GPU.

papers.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.authors_short: Luo, Jiang, Zhang, Zhu, Yu, Dominguez Silva, Zhou, Yuk, Zhou, Su
papers.venue: bioRxiv preprint ('contradictory results'), v1 posted 2026-06-17; reply to Collins et al. 2026
papers.code_status: no code release announced; the reply argues the method is fully specified in the 2024 paper
papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Luo et al. rebut: energy ratio 4 is an average muscle efficiency, not a ceiling (prior devices report 4.3-6.7); they compute 2.4 for walking; the replication used a fixed averaged torque curve, misread gait-phase timing, and a heavier 4.8 kg device.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: run a positive control first. The pipeline must reproduce an established result with a known controller before any 'does not reproduce' verdict; pre-register fidelity criteria (controller class, timing, device mass).
papers.left_untested: Reply announces no code, trained policy or seed release; cited independent successes (Barati 2026, others) are related methods, not replications, and were not verified here. Not peer-reviewed.
papers.feasibility_notes: Read with Collins et al.; its objections define the fidelity and positive-control checks a SMAT reconstruction must log.

papers.title: Deciphering the “Art” in Modeling and Simulation of the Knee Joint: Model Benchmarking
papers.authors_short: Nazem, Andreassen, Kim, Moyle, Besier, Halloran, Imhauser, Chokhandre, Schneider, Elmasry, Zaylor, Shelburne, Erdemir, Laz
papers.venue: Journal of Biomechanical Engineering 148(5):051004 (online 2026-02-05, issue May 2026)
papers.code_status: KneeHub data/model sharing not checked (simtk.org unreachable from this machine)
papers.api_title: Deciphering the “Art” in Modeling and Simulation of the Knee Joint: Model Benchmarking
papers.core_idea: KneeHub: five expert teams built and calibrated knee models from the same specimen data, then predicted unseen benchmark loadings. Major trends matched, but errors versus experiment (up to 13.5 deg internal-external rotation) and between-team spread were large; modeller decisions matter.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: score the reconstruction only on conditions never used for calibration or tuning (held-out speeds, subjects, tasks) and report between-implementation spread as part of reproduction uncertainty.
papers.left_untested: Knee joint mechanics with five teams; not whole-body musculoskeletal RL or exoskeletons, and no statistical criterion (e.g., equivalence margin) for calling a model reproduced.
papers.feasibility_notes: Emulate cheaply: two independent SMAT reimplementations (e.g., two agents working from the same text) give an implementation-spread estimate.

papers.title: Myths and methodologies: The use of equivalence and non-inferiority tests for interventional studies in exercise physiology and sport science
papers.api_title: Myths and methodologies: The use of equivalence and non‐inferiority tests for interventional studies in exercise physiology and sport science
papers.core_idea: Reviews how exercise physiology and sport science test interventions, then walks through designing and analysing equivalence and non-inferiority studies, including margin choice, sample size, analysis and reporting, with worked sport-science examples and recommendations.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: 'a simpler controller does the same' is an equivalence claim and 'SMAT is not worse' a non-inferiority claim; each needs its margin and seed count fixed by a pre-registered power calculation.
papers.left_untested: Human-subject trials only; no simulated agents, seeds or sweeps, and no margins for simulated sprint time or co-adaptation metrics.
papers.feasibility_notes: No compute; its margin-justification steps can be pasted into the pre-registration template.

papers.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
papers.api_title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
papers.core_idea: Optimising a noisy model-selection criterion overfits it; the resulting degradation can be as large as the differences between learning algorithms, and evaluating on data used for selection gives optimistically biased estimates. Nested protocols, with selection inside each evaluation split, avoid this.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: checkpoints, configs and stopping points are chosen on selection seeds by a pre-declared criterion; reported metrics come only from evaluation seeds never used in any selection step.
papers.left_untested: Kernel classifiers with cross-validation on fixed datasets; no RL, no non-stationary co-adaptation, and no guidance on how many candidates a sweep may compare.
papers.feasibility_notes: Costs only the held-out evaluation episodes; enforce with seed-set bookkeeping in the ledger.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning That Matters
papers.authors_short: Henderson, Islam, Bachman, Pineau, Precup, Meger
papers.venue: AAAI 2018 (Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 32(1))
papers.core_idea: Policy-gradient results on MuJoCo swing with random seeds, hyperparameters, network architecture, reward scale, environment and codebase; two seed groups of one algorithm can differ significantly. Calls for significance testing, all-seed reporting and standard protocols; Collins et al. cite it for convergence evidence.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: SMAT and every baseline share codebase, reward scale and network; seed count is fixed before running, and all-seed learning curves with intervals accompany every claim.
papers.left_untested: Four algorithms (TRPO, PPO, DDPG, ACKTR) on standard MuJoCo tasks; no musculoskeletal models, human-device coupling, or equivalence tests.
papers.feasibility_notes: Principles only; all-seed plots are free once the ledger stores per-seed curves.

papers.title: Reproducibility standards for machine learning in the life sciences
papers.authors_short: Heil, Hoffman, Markowetz, Lee, Greene, Hicks
papers.api_title: Reproducibility standards for machine learning in the life sciences
papers.core_idea: Proposes graded standards: bronze (data, models and code public), silver (plus one-command dependency install, documented run order, OS and resources, deterministic random components), gold (entire analysis reproducible with one command). Collins et al. cite it against Luo et al.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: target gold. One command rebuilds every reported number and figure from the append-only ledger on a clean second machine, with seeds set, environment pinned and run order recorded.
papers.left_untested: Short comment on life-science ML; does not address cross-hardware floating-point nondeterminism in GPU physics, so second-machine checks need a statistical tolerance rather than bitwise equality.
papers.feasibility_notes: Container or lockfile plus a single driver script; the second-machine rerun costs one extra run of each key result.

papers.title: The fundamental principles of reproducibility
papers.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 379(2197):20200210
papers.core_idea: Defines reproducibility from the scientific method: four types by what the original team shared (R1 description only, R2 code, R3 data, R4 full experiment) and three degrees (outcome, analysis, interpretation reproducible). The less that is shared, the more a successful reproduction generalises.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: label the SMAT reconstruction an R1 (description-only) study and state the degree each verdict reaches; never claim outcome-reproducible unless numbers match within the pre-set margin.
papers.left_untested: Conceptual taxonomy; no statistical test for each degree, and no treatment of partial reproductions or disputes over implementation fidelity such as Collins versus Luo.
papers.feasibility_notes: Zero cost; adopt its vocabulary in verdict templates and the paper package.

papers.title: Beyond “non-significant” results: Why and how to test for practical equivalence
papers.code_status: free online equivalence-test calculator introduced; URL not checked
papers.api_title: Beyond “non-significant” results: Why and how to test for practical equivalence
papers.core_idea: Non-significant comparisons (P ≥ 0.05) are routinely misreported as 'no difference'. Explains TOST logic, how it separates practical equivalence from inconclusive evidence, illustrates paired and unpaired comparisons, and introduces a free online equivalence calculator.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: verdicts have three states (equivalent, different, inconclusive), and the runner prints 'inconclusive' when neither test passes; use paired TOST when arms share evaluation seeds.
papers.left_untested: Only the abstract was checked; it covers single paired or unpaired comparisons, so multiplicity across sweeps and heavy-tailed seed distributions need other sources.
papers.feasibility_notes: Short read; the calculator can spot-check the runner's TOST implementation.

papers.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
papers.api_title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
papers.core_idea: Test-set scores alone mislead; report expected validation performance of the best-found model as a function of computation budget (hyperparameter trials or training time). Several published comparisons would reverse with more or less compute; ends with reporting best practices.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: equal-budget comparisons. Log every trial, plot expected best performance against number of trials for SMAT and each baseline, and compare arms at the same declared budget.
papers.left_untested: NLP models with validation sets; RL returns are noisy per seed, and the estimator assumes i.i.d. trials, which staged or population-based tuning violates.
papers.feasibility_notes: Computed from the trial log; no extra runs.

papers.title: Sustainable computational science: the ReScience initiative
papers.authors_short: Rougier, Hinsen, Alexandre, Arildsen et al.
papers.code_status: journal infrastructure on GitHub (continued as ReScience C)
papers.api_title: Sustainable computational science: the ReScience initiative
papers.core_idea: Introduces ReScience, a GitHub-hosted journal for independent open-source re-implementations of published computational studies from their description. Submissions explain why they replicated or failed; two reviewers test and evaluate the code; editors note authors rarely submit failed replications.
papers.what_to_take: Rule: the paper package is a replication report: original claims, every reimplementation decision filling gaps in the description, all outcomes including failures, and runnable code; partial replications must be justified.
papers.left_untested: Publication workflow, not statistics; what counts as 'similar enough to be considered equivalent' is left to each field.
papers.feasibility_notes: ReScience C and MLRC 2026 (TMLR proceedings, NeurIPS track) both accept failed reproductions; plausible venues for the final package.

cluster_lessons: A reproduction of a paper without code is an R1 (description-only) study: when it fails, the cause is hard to locate, so fix fidelity criteria and a positive control before running (Gundersen 2021; Rougier et al. 2017; Luo et al. 2026).

The Collins-Luo exchange shows how a negative exoskeleton result gets attacked: controller fidelity (fixed torque vs learned policy), gait timing, device mass and whether its penalty was measured separately, and the basis of the plausibility bound. Pre-register a check for each.

'Does not reproduce' and 'a simpler controller does the same' are interval claims: TOST or non-inferiority with margins fixed in raw units beforehand. A non-significant difference is inconclusive, not 'same' (Lakens et al. 2018; Mazzolari et al. 2022; Tomek et al. 2026).

Selection is the main hidden bias: choose configs and checkpoints on tuning seeds, rerun the frozen choice on fresh seeds, and report only that rerun (Patterson et al. 2024; Eimer et al. 2023; Cawley & Talbot 2010).
Report every seed with bootstrap intervals and robust aggregates; two seed groups of the same algorithm can differ 'significantly' by chance (Henderson et al. 2018; Agarwal et al. 2021).
Compare arms at equal, declared tuning budgets: conclusions can flip with budget, as Dodge et al. 2019 show and as Patterson et al. 2024's 30-seed SAC-vs-DDPG re-run illustrates.
Expert teams given identical data still diverge (KneeHub, Nazem et al. 2026): treat between-implementation spread as a floor on reproduction uncertainty and score only on held-out conditions.

Critics now invoke code-release standards (Heil et al. 2021 gold: one command reproduces everything). Build the paper package from the ledger that way and rerun key results on a second machine with a statistical, not bitwise, tolerance.
occupied_claims: Collins et al. 2026 (preprint) already report a failed N=10 hardware replication of Luo et al. 2024's walking torque profile plus an energy-ratio implausibility argument; cite it, do not headline 'simulation-learned exoskeleton gains fail to replicate' as new.
Luo et al. 2026 already argue that energy ratios above 4 occur in prior devices and that fixed-torque replications do not test learned policies.
Henderson et al. 2018, Colas et al. 2018, Agarwal et al. 2021 and Patterson et al. 2024 already establish that few-seed deep-RL comparisons are unreliable and how reporting should change.
Eimer et al. 2023 already show that RL hyperparameters overfit the tuning seeds and that tuning and test seeds must be separated.
Patterson et al. 2024 already re-ran a published RL comparison (SAC vs DDPG, 30 seeds) and reached different conclusions from the original.
KneeHub (Andreassen et al. 2023; Nazem et al. 2026) already quantified multi-team divergence when modelling the same knee data.
open_gaps: No independent, pre-registered reproduction of a musculoskeletal-RL human-exoskeleton co-adaptation method (SMAT or similar) was found; a TOST-based SMAT reproduction with positive and negative controls would be new.
No plausibility bound exists for simulated sprint-time gains analogous to the walking energy-ratio argument; deriving one (device work vs time saved) is open and cheap in simulation.

No field consensus on equivalence margins for simulated metabolic cost or sprint time; the programme must justify its own (e.g., from the original effect size or the simulator's seed-to-seed noise floor).
No accepted criterion for declaring an RL reproduction failed when the original reports few seeds or no variance; small-telescopes-style rules (Simonsohn 2015) have not been tested on RL.
RL evaluation guides do not address multiplicity control for an unattended agent running many pre-registered tests (alpha spending across a queue).
Second-machine reproduction of GPU physics plus RL has no standard tolerance; the programme must pre-set one (e.g., TOST between machines on the key metric).
unverifiable: Seed 'any 2023-2026 reproducibility study in musculoskeletal RL': none found via Crossref, OpenAlex and three web searches; the nearest are Collins et al. 2026 (exoskeleton control) and KneeHub 2026 (knee modelling). Absence is not proven.

Independent learning-in-simulation exoskeleton results cited by Luo et al. 2026 (Barati et al. 2026 RA-L; Zhou et al. 2025; Park et al. 2026; others) were not verified; they are related methods, not replications.

Luo et al. 2026 state that Collins et al. was submitted to Nature as a Matters Arising in December 2025 and was under review when posted; this comes from one party and was not independently confirmed.
Tomek et al. 2026: only the Crossref record and abstract were seen; the calculator URL and full text were not checked.
Tool limits: Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 and DBLP and proceedings.mlsys.org were unreachable by curl; the MLSys 2021 listing for Bouthillier et al. was confirmed through WebFetch instead.
